questions.q: What real, three-step pattern does the `transfer` function follow?
options: Subtract from the sender's balance, add to the recipient's balance, emit Transfer
Emit Transfer first, then update balances
Only update the recipient's balance
Check the allowance, then update balances
questions.explain: transfer subtracts the amount from the sender, adds it to the recipient, then emits Transfer to log the change.

questions.q: What real mechanism does `transferFrom` enable that plain `transfer` cannot?
options: Moving tokens on someone else's behalf, once they've approved you to do so
Deleting a token holder's balance entirely
Transferring tokens without ever checking any balance
Minting brand new tokens
questions.explain: transferFrom lets a third party (the approved spender) move tokens from an owner's balance — the real mechanism behind delegated spending.

questions.q: Why does `transferFrom` deduct from the allowance before touching either balance?
options: To make the function cost less gas overall
The order doesn't actually matter at all
Allowances are unrelated to transferFrom entirely
So the transaction reverts if the caller wasn't approved for enough, before any balance actually changes
questions.explain: Checking (and deducting) the allowance first ensures an unauthorized or over-limit call fails safely, before any real balance is modified.

questions.q: What does calling `approve(spender, amount)` actually do?
options: Immediately transfers amount tokens to spender
Sets allowance[msg.sender][spender] to amount and emits an Approval event
Deletes the caller's entire token balance
Mints amount new tokens for the spender
questions.explain: approve only records how much a spender is allowed to move later — it doesn't move any tokens itself.

questions.q: What real value does every one of these three functions return upon success?
options: The new total supply
Nothing — these functions have no return value
true — the standard ERC-20 convention confirming the operation succeeded
The caller's remaining balance
questions.explain: transfer, approve, and transferFrom all return a boolean, with true signaling that the call executed successfully, per the ERC-20 standard.
